questions.stem: Which of the following contains genetic information?
questions.solution: Chromatin is the structure that contains DNA, which carries genetic information. The nucleolus is involved in ribosome production, ribosomes are responsible for protein synthesis, and the nuclear membrane is a protective barrier around the nucleus. Therefore, chromatin is the only option that directly contains genetic information.

questions.stem: Why do mature Red Blood Cells (RBCs) in humans not have a nucleus?
choices: To provide more space for haemoglobin
questions.solution: Mature red blood cells lack a nucleus to create more space for haemoglobin, which is essential for oxygen transport. The presence of a nucleus would take up space that could otherwise be used for more haemoglobin molecules. Options like storing more oxygen or increasing lifespan are not directly related to the absence of a nucleus, and allowing cell division is incorrect because mature RBCs cannot divide.

questions.stem: What is the main function of the cell membrane?
choices: To provide structural support to the cell
To control the movement of substances in and out of the cell
To produce energy for the cell
questions.solution: The cell membrane controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell. It is selectively permeable, allowing some substances to pass through while blocking others. The other options describe functions of other cell structures, such as the cell wall or mitochondria.

questions.stem: What is the process by which water moves across a selectively permeable membrane?
questions.solution: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from an area of higher water concentration to an area of lower water concentration. Diffusion is the movement of particles, not specifically water. Active transport and photosynthesis are unrelated processes.

questions.stem: A student uses a light microscope with an eyepiece magnification of 10X and an objective lens of 40X. If the estimated size of a cell is 200 μm, what is the total magnification of the microscope?
questions.solution: The total magnification of a microscope is calculated by multiplying the magnification of the eyepiece and the objective lens. Here, the eyepiece is 10X and the objective lens is 40X, so 10 × 40 = 400X. The option '10X' is the eyepiece magnification only. '40X' is the objective lens magnification only. '50X' is an incorrect addition of the two magnifications.

hi.solution: सूक्ष्मदर्शी का कुल आवर्धन नेत्र लेंस और लेंस के आवर्धन को गुणा करके गणना की जाती है। यहां, नेत्र लेंस 10X है और लेंस 40X है, इसलिए 10 × 40 = 400X। विकल्प '10X' केवल नेत्र लेंस आवर्धन है। '40X' केवल लेंस आवर्धन है। '50X' दोनों आवर्धन का गलत जोड़ है।

questions.stem: Which cell organelles are involved in the synthesis of the cell membrane?
questions.solution: The cell membrane is made up of proteins and lipids, and the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi complex are responsible for their synthesis and transport. Lysosomes are involved in breaking down materials, mitochondria produce energy, and the nucleus contains genetic material. The correct answer is the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi complex.

questions.stem: In an experiment, two similar animal cells are placed in two different solutions: Cell X is placed in pure water and Cell Y is placed in a concentrated salt solution. After some time, Cell X swells and Cell Y shrinks. What is the correct explanation for this observation?
choices: Salt molecules moved into Cell Y, causing it to shrink
Water moved into Cell X and more water moved out of Cell Y than the salt solution entered in it
Water moved into Cell X and moved out of Cell Y through the cell membrane
Solute movement caused osmosis in both cells
questions.solution: Osmosis is the movement of water across a semi-permeable membrane from an area of lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration. In pure water, water moves into Cell X, causing it to swell. In a concentrated salt solution, water moves out of Cell Y, causing it to shrink. The other options incorrectly describe the direction of solute or water movement.

questions.stem: A student observes that in a plant, a single mature cell can develop into a complete plant under suitable conditions. Which of the following best explains this observation?
choices: The cell has the ability to divide and differentiate into all cell types
The cell contains only a single chromosome
The cell is not affected by external conditions
The cell is not part of a tissue
questions.solution: The correct answer is that the cell has the ability to divide and differentiate into all cell types. This is because a single cell can give rise to all the different cell types needed for a complete plant, a process known as totipotency. The other options are incorrect because a single chromosome would not provide the full genetic information needed, external conditions are not irrelevant but necessary for growth, and being part of a tissue does not explain the cell's developmental potential.

questions.stem: Why do plant cells not shrink when placed in a concentrated sugar solution, while animal cells do?
choices: Because plant cells have a cell wall
Because plant cells are more rigid
Because plant cells have a higher concentration of water

questions.solution: The correct answer is because plant cells have a cell wall. Animal cells lack a cell wall, so they shrink when placed in a hypertonic solution. The other options are not the main reason for the difference in behavior.

questions.stem: What is the function of ribosomes in a cell?
questions.solution: Ribosomes are responsible for synthesising proteins, as they read genetic instructions and assemble amino acids into proteins. questions.stem: Which of the following is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms?
questions.solution: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms because all life forms are composed of one or more cells, and cells carry out all necessary life processes. Tissue is a group of similar cells, an organ is made of different tissues, and a system is a group of organs working together, none of which are the fundamental unit of life.

questions.stem: What is the function of the cell membrane?
questions.solution: The cell membrane controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell, maintaining the cell's internal environment. Providing structural rigidity is a function of the cell wall, not the membrane. Storing genetic material is the role of the nucleus, and carrying out photosynthesis is the function of chloroplasts in plant cells.

questions.stem: In which type of cell division are two genetically identical daughter cells produced?
questions.solution: Mitosis is the type of cell division that produces two genetically identical daughter cells from one parent cell. Meiosis produces gametes with half the number of chromosomes, binary fission is a type of cell division in prokaryotes, and mitochondrial division is a separate process for replicating mitochondria.

questions.stem: If a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, what will happen to the cell?
questions.solution: In a hypertonic solution, the concentration of solutes outside the cell is higher than inside, so water moves out of the cell to balance the concentration. This loss of water causes the cell to shrink. Swelling or bursting would occur in a hypotonic solution, and remaining the same would happen in an isotonic solution.

questions.stem: If a cell is placed in a solution where the concentration of solutes is equal inside and outside the cell, what will happen to the cell?
questions.solution: When the concentration of solutes is equal inside and outside the cell, there is no net movement of water across the cell membrane, so the cell maintains its size and shape. In this scenario, the cell remains the same because there is no osmotic pressure causing it to swell or shrink. Swelling or bursting occurs in a hypotonic solution, while shrinking happens in a hypertonic solution.

questions.stem: What is the main function of mitosis?
choices: To produce gametes for sexual reproduction
To create genetic diversity among organisms
To produce two genetically identical daughter cells
To reduce the number of chromosomes in a cell
questions.solution: Mitosis results in two cells that are genetically identical to the original cell, which is essential for growth and tissue repair. Gametes are produced through meiosis, not mitosis, and genetic diversity arises from meiosis due to processes like crossing over. Reducing chromosome number is also a feature of meiosis, not mitosis.

क्योंकि यह सभी जीवों में पाई जाती है
क्योंकि यह एक जीव में सबसे बड़ी इकाई है
hi.solution: सही उत्तर यह है कि यह सभी जीवन प्रक्रियाओं को कर सकने वाली सबसे छोटी इकाई है। ऐसा इसलिए है क्योंकि कोशिकाएं अपने आप वृद्धि, प्रजनन और एंजाइम के रूप में महत्वपूर्ण कार्य कर सकती हैं। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि सभी कोशिकाएं स्वतंत्र रूप से जीवित नहीं रह सकतीं, और कोशिका एक जीव में सबसे बड़ी इकाई नहीं है। यद्यपि कोशिकाएं सभी जीवों में पाई जाती हैं, लेकिन उनकी परिभाषा उनकी जीवन प्रक्रियाओं को करने की क्षमता है।

questions.stem: Why do plant cells have a large central vacuole while animal cells do not?
choices: Because plant cells need to store more food
Because plant cells require more water for turgor pressure
Because animal cells have more organelles
Because animal cells are smaller in size
questions.solution: Plant cells have a large central vacuole to maintain turgor pressure, which helps keep the plant upright. Animal cells do not need this because they have other structural supports. The other options do not explain the primary reason for the presence of a large vacuole in plant cells.

questions.stem: What is the main reason that complex multicellular organisms cannot be reconstructed from a single cell?
choices: They have a complex structure that cannot be replicated
They require specialized cells organized into tissues and organs
They are made up of non-living cells
They have a nucleus that is too large
questions.solution: The main reason complex multicellular organisms cannot be reconstructed from a single cell is that they require specialized cells organized into tissues and organs, which a single cell cannot provide. Other options are incorrect because cells in these organisms are living, and a nucleus's size does not prevent reconstruction. The complexity of their structure is due to cell specialization, not an inability to replicate.
